# Corpus Mining: Maja D'Aoust, *The Occult I Ching: The Secret Language of Serpents* (Destiny Books, 2019)

Source PDF: `/mnt/agents/upload/_OceanofPDF.com_The_Occult_1_Ching_The_secret_language_of_serpents_-_Maja_D_Aoust.pdf` (450 PDF pages; uncorrected proofs).
Page citations = **printed book pages** (PDF page − 11, calibrated: Hexagram 1 = printed p. 43). ±2.

**Character of the book:** narrative/philosophical rather than tabular. Part 1 = serpent/daimon/DNA theory; Part 2 = 64 hexagram entries with original artwork, each with a fixed header block. Unlike Wen, D'Aoust has **no systematic trigram attribute tables** (no direction/season/color grids); her correspondence systems are (a) hexagram→tarot card (one per hexagram), (b) hexagram→oracle-bone script image (her readings of the ancient glyphs), (c) DNA codons↔hexagrams (quoting Stent/Yan), (d) serpent/daimon cross-cultural parallels.

## 1. SMALLEST FRAGMENTS

| # | Fragment | Definition / evidence |
|---|----------|----------------------|
| F1 | **Yin / Yang** | "Yin is female, dark, cold, earth, and yang is male, light, hot, heaven. These are more energetic than literal. Energy manifests as two polar extremes and then a combination of the two, which forms the Tao" (p. 35). |
| F2 | **Line (yao), four kinds** | "Each line of your hexagram will be one of four possibilities: yin that doesn't change, yin that changes, yang that doesn't change, and yang that changes. Yin lines are written as broken, and yang lines are unbroken" (p. 35). Changing yin marked X, changing yang marked O (or a dot) (p. 36). |
| F3 | **Gua 卦** | "Gua means something like 'oracle symbol' or 'archetype,' like a representative or scapegoat. It also means to divine, to tell fortunes, or to read fates" (p. 17). "In some of the ancient texts, the gua were a type of dragon, supernatural spirit, or familiar who could confer special powers to humans… the gua are daimons who constitute the divinations and are the sources of information" (p. 17). |
| F4 | **The eight bagua** | Listed with Japanese + pinyin names: ☰ ken/qian, ☱ da/dui, ☲ ri/li, ☳ shin/zhen, ☴ son/xun, ☵ kan/kan, ☶ gon/gen, ☷ kon/kun (p. 16). Discovered by Fu Xi on a tortoise shell in the Yellow River (p. 8). |
| F5 | **Yi 易 (change)** | "'Yi'… usually translated as change… Philosophically, Yi is primordial change, the mutations of transformations that initiate the process of generation and transformation in all the myriad beings" (Karcher, quoted p. 27–28). "Yi can also mean mobility or fluidity" (p. 21). Character for yi "really looks like a section of DNA undergoing 'change' or transcription" (p. 27). |
| F6 | **Ching 經** | "means a loom containing a warp and weft" (p. 28); daimons = gaps/openings in the loom (kairos), via Karcher/Eliade (pp. 26–28). |
| F7 | **Daimon** | Core primitive: Greek daiesthai/daiomai = "to divide, distribute, allot" — "When we consult the I Ching, we divide yarrow sticks into lots, and so the daimon becomes our lot in life" (p. 19). Jung: "a psychic force, a transformational energy and source of images that cuts across boundaries" (p. 18). Frager: archetype = "form without content… a pattern through which energy may flow" (p. 19). |
| F8 | **Hexagram = 64 permutations** | "The I Ching is made of the sixty-four permutations of the eight bagua" (p. 17). Built bottom-up "like constructing a house. The first line will be the foundation, and the last line will be the roof" (p. 35). |
| F9 | **Shadow line (fan yao 反爻)** | "Each line has its shadow line, which transforms the line into its opposite. Look up the shadow line for each line you draw at the indicated hexagram number and line locations (44.1, for instance…)" — every changing-line entry ends "u Transforms into Shadow NN.n" (p. 38; e.g., Hex 1 line 1 → shadow 44.1, p. 46). |
| F10 | **Relating hexagram** | Changed lines generate "an entire second hexagram… This is your relating hexagram, or what the situation is becoming or heading toward" (p. 36). |
| F11 | **"All lines changing" state** | Each hexagram entry has an all-lines-changing section: "a different overall meaning is generated than if only one of the lines underwent a transformation… the transformation will be more profound" (p. 38). |
| F12 | **Fu Xi sequence vs King Wen sequence** | "ways of organizing the hexagrams that change the algorithms when you are performing the reading" (p. 40). |
| F13 | **Serpent** | The meta-primitive: Fu Xi half-serpent; Hebrew nachash = serpent AND "to divine/prognosticate" (Strong's Concordance quoted, p. 12); Delphic python; Egyptian Poimandres "Great Dragon" who answers Hermes' questions (pp. 13–15); nagas; Fu Xi + Nü Wa intertwined serpent bodies "much like DNA" (p. 9). |
| F14 | **Golden ratio / phi** | "All things in nature contain one repeated pattern—the golden rectangle of phi—which means that we find ourselves in a limited number of experiences" (Intro, p. 4); I Ching as labyrinth thread "of the golden ratio" (p. 41). |
| F15 | **Four base yin-yang combinations** | referenced as generating "a little over ten thousand potential responses" — tied to Tao Te Ching "three becomes the ten thousand things" (p. 40). |

### C2. DNA ↔ I Ching (pp. 24–31)
- Stent (1969, *The Coming of the Golden Age*): "if Yang is identified with the purine bases and Yin with pyrimidine bases, so that old Yang and Yin correspond to the complementary adenine and Thymine pair and new Yin and Yang to the complementary guanine and cytosine pair, each of the 64 hexagrams comes to represent one of the nucleotide triplet codons" (p. 24). [Note: differs from Johnson Yan's mapping quoted by Wen — two rival correspondences.]
- Yan, *DNA and the I Ching: The Tao of Life*: "Both DNA and the I Ching are based upon a binary quaternary code that generates a system of 64 possibilities… in the I Ching, hexagrams change into other hexagrams through the interchange of yin and yang lines; in DNA, point mutations occur through changes in the nucleotide bases" (p. 25).
- DNA repair = the "gap" mechanic: "gaps in DNA spur it to change and evolve… this is where evolution takes place" — paralleled with daimon-as-gap (pp. 26–27).
- F. A. Popp: "The genetic Yi Ching provides such a 'periodic system of the spiritual element,' and acts as a goal for human evolution" (p. 31).
- Leibniz/Bouvet binary (pp. 25–26, 410–411).

### C3. Serpent ↔ divination cross-cultural lexicon (pp. 8–15)
nachash (Hebrew: serpent/enchanter/diviner) ↔ wu 巫 (Chinese shaman/"witch") ↔ Pythia/python (Delphi) ↔ nagas (India/Tibet; Nagarjuna) ↔ Poimandres–Thoth/Hermes (Egypt) ↔ Fu Xi/Nü Wa (China). Augury/august/aureate (Au=gold) light-etymology cluster (p. 9).

### C4. Fu Xi & Nü Wa ↔ Freemasonry
"The two were depicted as an intertwined pair whose lower serpent bodies formed an interspiraling shape, much like DNA… Fu Xi and Nü Wa hold in their hands the iconic symbols of the compass and the ruler, now recognized in Freemasonry buildings across the globe" (p. 9). Compass+ruler = feng shui/star-survey instruments.

### C5. I Ching ↔ Lo Shu / Saturn magic square
"The I Ching is like a magic puzzle box. It is a living Lo Shu magic number square, much like the Saturn magic square magicians have used in Western occult traditions" (p. 41).

### C6. Healing & martial arts correspondences (pp. 21–23)
- Chinese medicine: gua ↔ "five-element theory of the zhang-fu organ system" (p. 22); Huang Di Nei Jing philosophically based on Fu Xi's gua; Fu Xi credited with inventing the acupuncture needle. Medical maxim: "where there is stagnation there is pain" (Tong zi tong bu tong zi tong, p. 21) — I Ching "removes clots of stagnant daimons" as acupuncture removes qi stagnation.
- Martial arts: gua ↔ "different body postures or poses… a system of movement"; "sufficient evidence points to many qigong masters specifically deriving the postures of the physical body directly from the bagua"; Bruce Lee's jeet kune do philosophy (bend and spring back; yin-yang moderation) (pp. 22–23).

### C7. I Ching ↔ AI / computing (appendix, pp. 410–420)
"The I Ching can be thought of as a way to interface with reality" (p. 411); "since the I Ching mimics and recapitulates much of the DNA sequencing and math it can also be said to act as a DNA computer" (p. 411); "I Ching is an AI training ground provided by daimons to graduate us into a new level of conscious existence" (p. 413); casting a gua = "repeating the act of creation itself… a microcosm of how the DNA of sperm and egg united to make a zygote" (p. 413). Leibniz Monadology cited for sentience (p. 416).

**Negative results for D'Aoust:** no color/direction/season grids, no wuxing generation/conquest tables, no stems/branches, no pitch-pipes, no King Wen vs Fu Xi arrangement diagrams (mentioned only), no yarrow step-by-step.

## 3. RULES

### R1. Coin method (pp. 34–37)
- Three coins, any kind; six throws; hexagram built bottom-up (foundation→roof).
- Values: 3 tails = changing yin; 3 heads = changing yang; 2 tails + 1 head = unchanging yin; 2 heads + 1 tail = unchanging yang. [Same convention as Wen's Meaning & Principle column.]
- Mark changing lines with X (yin) or O (yang) or a dot.
- Changing lines flip to opposites → relating hexagram (no changing lines in second hexagram).
- Historical method note: heated turtle shells read by crack patterns (origin); yarrow = "drawing of lots."

### R2. Reading protocol (pp. 37–38)
- Read general hexagram meaning + only the changing lines drawn ("Your changing line(s) is the one that applies directly to you").
- Look up the shadow line (fan yao) of each changing line too ("allowing you to see the issue in more of a totality").
- Read the relating hexagram as "potential capacities or navigational directions" — NOT as fixed future: "I would advise against such predictive divinations because they exclude growth and free will" (p. 36).
- All-lines-changing → read the special "all lines changing" section (transformation more profound).

### R3. Line-position lenses (her six-place grammar, pp. 37–38)
- Line 1 = the Self ("something you yourself need to do")
- Line 2 = the Other (people around you, their perspective)
- Line 3 = unification/rectifier (align self with other/environment)
- Line 4 = Earth (transpersonal, larger view)
- Line 5 = conflict (external obstacles; strategy/technique)
- Line 6 = view from above (Heaven's spiritual perspective; transcendence)

### R4. Question craft & conduct rules (pp. 34–35, 40–41)
- Articulate the question carefully ("A good detective can solve a case if he asks the right question"); any question allowed, or none ("ask about 'now'").
- Ritual optional but focusing: "Setting up a ritual is a good way to focus your mind."
- Anti-compulsion rule: "do not sit there doing readings over and over… you must never abandon your autonomy to anything, or you risk illness and a loss of integrity. Decide upon your own actions, and think of all oracles as advice from a friend" (p. 40).
- Discernment rule: "The secret of the I Ching is to pay attention to your reaction to it… you do not need to agree with it; you only need to listen to your own response to the draw" (pp. 41–42).

### R5. Hexagram manipulation toolkit (via Karcher, p. 40)
"ways to manipulate the hexagrams to generate the seasons, interior hexagrams, and shadow hexagrams"; hexagrams can "generate specific dates and times and even geographical locations" (feng shui usage); plum blossom method for timing (citing Alfred Huang).

## 4. SYNTAX / STRATA

### S1. Hexagram entry template (Part 2, decoded on pp. 38–39)
Fixed strata per hexagram: (1) number (from gua sequence); (2) English name + Chinese name; (3) yin/yang line figure ("elements and nature of the gua"); (4) Oracle Script = her reading of the ancient turtle-shell glyph; (5) motto quote + keyword (e.g., "Creative Conception," "As Above So Below," "Contact with the muse"); (6) Tarot card; (7) in-depth description (cross-cultural myth weaving: e.g., Hex 1 = Ruach Elohim, breath of God, pp. 43–45); (8) Guru = spiritual lesson; (9) Personal Example = observed answer-patterns from practice; (10) The Changing Lines: six entries labeled Line One—The Self … Line Six, each ending "u Transforms into Shadow NN.n"; (11) All-lines-changing section.

### S2. Formulaic elements
No omen-phrase glossary (吉/凶 etc.) — she deliberately deliteralizes: quoting Karcher, "the oracle's signifiers are complex networks of meaning related to dream-images, which disfigure everyday language" (p. 18). Hexagram 1 glosses qian as "dynamic tension… a string pulled taut, like a guitar string that, when tightened, yields a specific tone" + Schuessler etymology "to lead by hand, drag along, stretch out or tighten a rope" (p. 43–45). Mottos function as her valence layer.

### S3. Xi-Ci-Zhuan on consultation grammar (quoted p. 17)
"The sage has seen the complex things in the world and imaged them in forms and symbols. Thus those forms and symbols are called images… In performing a proper ritual, he can append his judgements of fortune and misfortune to lines of the gua… To simulate before speaking, to reflect before acting."

## 6. BIGGEST FINDINGS (D'Aoust)

1. **A complete, original hexagram→tarot assignment for all 64 hexagrams** (C1) — a full state-to-state cross-mapping between the 64-state I Ching and 78-state tarot, orthogonal to both Wen's and Crowley's systems. Includes per-hexagram motto keywords usable as valence labels.
2. **Shadow-line (fan yao) operator made explicit for every line** (F9) — a formal negation/opposition transform with lookup notation (NN.n), giving the state space a built-in involution.
3. **The serpent-as-divination-language thesis** (C3): nachash/wu/Pythia/Poimandres/Fu Xi — divination systems personified as serpent-daimons; the oracle = "sacred language" (Karcher) spoken between human and spirit; directly supports a "Language/Symbol" primitive class.
4. **DNA↔hexagram correspondence with two rival mappings documented** (Stent purine/pyrimidine vs. Yan) + the gap/repair mechanic as an evolution trigger — a candidate model for state-space mutation operators.
5. **I Ching as interface/AI (C7)**: casting a hexagram = microcosm of zygote formation; the oracle as sentient interface — her framing of the 64 states as a *simulation container* ("AI training ground provided by daimons").
